title: $L^2$ norm squared as a self inner product
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean hypercube, and equip such functions with the uniform-measure inner product $\langle g, h \rangle = 2^{-n}\sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} g(x)\,h(x)$. Then the squared $L^2$ norm of $f$ equals the inner product of $f$ with itself:
\[
  \|f\|_2^2 \;=\; \langle f, f \rangle.
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a real-valued function on the Boolean hypercube of dimension n
replaced:
For every $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the locally-defined squared $L^2$ norm agrees
with the upstream inner product of $f$ with itself:
\[
  \|f\|_2^2 \;=\; \langle f, f \rangle_{\mathbb{B}}.
\]
